includedPullRequests.title: Watch: fewer, better-timed state updates
includedPullRequests.body:
## Summary

The phone rebuilt and resent the whole watch state far more often than needed: on every new reading, every loop, every IOB change and every write that only set an upload flag, and it queued each snapshot with `transferUserInfo`, so a backgrounded watch worked through a backlog of outdated states. This PR sends fewer and better-timed updates and fixes a few bugs on the way. The data sent to the watch stays as on dev.

## What's new

### Fewer, better-timed pushes
- **Upload flags ignored:** new `CoreDataStack.contentChangePublisher`, like `entityChangePublisher` without updates that only set `isUploadedToNS` / `isUploadedToHealth` / `isUploadedToTidepool`. Used by the Apple Watch and the Garmin manager.
- **Coalesced:** every trigger (glucose, IOB, determination, override, temp target, settings) goes through `scheduleWatchStatePush()`. The first trigger starts a 0.5 s window; triggers inside it join that push instead of delaying it. While a loop is running it holds the push until the result is in, capped at 30 s so a slow pump can't delay the BG value.
- `setupWatchState()` returns `nil` instead of an empty placeholder state, which the watch would have shown. Reachability is no longer required to build it: `isReachable` is only true while the watch app is in the foreground, and the context is what reaches it otherwise. There is no backlog, since the context holds only the newest state.

### Transport
- `transferUserInfo` → `updateApplicationContext`: only the newest state is kept, no backlog. It is also what reaches a watch app that isn't running, so a backgrounded watch and its complications stay current.
- Watch requests use `sendMessage` with a reply. The phone answers with the state directly through a new `didReceiveMessage(_:replyHandler:)` (every path replies; an empty reply means no state) and updates the context with it. A watch app not yet updated still asks without a reply handler; it gets the state pushed, as on dev.
- The phone no longer pushes when the watch becomes reachable: the watch asks itself, and only one request is in flight at a time (a second one waits for the reply or the 10 s timeout).

### Watch app
- `WatchState.shared` singleton. Before, every view re-init created a new instance that took over the weak session delegate and was then released, leaving nothing to receive from the phone.
- If the session is already activated at launch, it is handled right away (the activation callback won't come) and `receivedApplicationContext` is applied. The app also refreshes when its scene becomes active.
- In the background a received state is applied right away instead of after the debounce, because watchOS suspends the app before a delayed work item runs. On leaving the foreground a pending state is applied.
- Duplicate detection is in memory (`lastAcceptedStateDate`) instead of a timestamp saved to disk, so a payload is never dropped as a duplicate of one a previous launch showed. `WatchStateSnapshot` is removed on both sides.
- A stale state's glucose readings are still taken over when they are newer; its IOB, COB and trend are not.
- The BG bubble is dated by the newest reading's age (over 6 min) instead of the last update. IOB, COB and the treatment buttons stay on the last update (over 5 min) as on dev, so a CGM gap doesn't block treatments. A 30 s timer and a refresh when the app becomes active keep both current. The text under the bubble still shows the loop's age, as on dev.
- The syncing animation only shows when a request was actually sent, and is hidden after 10 s without an answer or when the request fails.

### Fixes
- The BG target was read asynchronously in `init`, so the watch sometimes got the default of 100. It is now read on each build.

includedPullRequests.title: Fix Apple Watch bolus direction arrow
includedPullRequests.body:
Add tests and validate that the bolus crown wheel animation shows the arrow in the correct appropriate direction. - **Target:** simulator - **Commit:** `f6a0532a0b` Point the watch bolus crown hint arrow by crown side, not wrist - **Xcode:** 26.2 · **Result:** passed - **Full report:** https://github.com/jwoglom/trio-test-harness/actions/runs/43893036686 Tested all 4 wrist/crown combinations on the bolus Confirm screen. A (wrist=L,crown=R): clockwise, expected clockwise, MATCH. B (wrist=L,crown=L): counterclockwise, expected counterclockwise, MATCH. C (wrist=R,crown=L): counterclockwise, expected counterclockwise, MATCH. D (wrist=R,crown=R): clockwise, expected clockwise, MATCH. All 4 bolus requests (0.1 U each) confirmed via crown turn and verified received by the Pump Simulator in Trio logs and phone UI. #### ✅ Works as expected | | | | |---|---|---| | ![Setup A (wrist left, crown right): Confirm screen shows the clockwise crown-hint arrow, matching expectation.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d7bb5bef-02e0-40a7-be31-b292c8c499ab)
Setup A (wrist left, crown right): Confirm screen shows the clockwise crown-hint arrow, matching expectation. | ![Setup A: phone's Pump Simulator chart shows the 0.1 U bolus delivered after the crown turn confirmed it.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6d6f075d-0808-459e-bf56-60a9be1540d6)
Setup A: phone's Pump Simulator chart shows the 0.1 U bolus delivered after the crown turn confirmed it. | ![Setup B (wrist left, crown left): Confirm screen shows the counterclockwise arrow, matching expectation despite sharing the same wrist as setup A.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cc2a8755-9ad4-44bc-a0bc-065beab58cd1)
Setup B (wrist left, crown left): Confirm screen shows the counterclockwise arrow, matching expectation despite sharing the same wrist as setup A. | | ![Setup B: after a negative crown delta (the positive one had no effect), IOB rises to 0.2 U, confirming the second bolus was sent.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/129961f6-9930-4717-975c-d6f4d17d3c0c)
Setup B: after a negative crown delta (the positive one had no effect), IOB rises to 0.2 U, confirming the second bolus was sent. | ![Setup C (wrist right, crown left): Confirm screen shows the counterclockwise arrow, matching expectation.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fbec2187-57c4-4dac-86cf-3b710885006f)
Setup C (wrist right, crown left): Confirm screen shows the counterclockwise arrow, matching expectation. | ![Setup C: after the crown turn, watch IOB rises to 0.3 U, confirming the third bolus was sent.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/761017f9-7457-4128-b29f-2cb604031895)
Setup C: after the crown turn, watch IOB rises to 0.3 U, confirming the third bolus was sent. | | ![Setup D (wrist right, crown right): Confirm screen shows the clockwise arrow, matching expectation and contradicting the PR text's predicted known-issue mismatch for this case.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/38663b4c-4540-4bf5-b0f2-a3897e35a837)
Setup D (wrist right, crown right): Confirm screen shows the clockwise arrow, matching expectation and contradicting the PR text's predicted known-issue mismatch for this case. | ![Setup D: phone's Pump Simulator chart shows cumulative 0.4 U delivered after all four boluses, confirming the final one was received.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a3eab998-b19d-4778-888b-fd844dee9b29)
Setup D: phone's Pump Simulator chart shows cumulative 0.4 U delivered after all four boluses, confirming the final one was received. | | 8 of 27 screenshots chosen by a separate review pass; all steps are in the [full report](https://github.com/jwoglom/trio-test-harness/actions/runs/43893036686).
